newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK retirement fund inflow seen at HK$40 bln in Y1.
newsitem.headline: HK retirement fund inflow seen at HK$40 bln in Y1.

text.p: New fund flows into Hong Kong's proposed Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) are expected to amount to about HK$40 billion in the first year of operation, a leading fund manager said on Thursday.

"The MPF will result in some 2.5 million Hong Kong employees becoming members of retirement schemes for the very first time," Stuart Leckie, chairman of Fidelity Investments Asia Pacific, told a news conference.

Leckie, who also chairs the newly-formed industry organisation, the Hong Kong Retirement Scheme Association, said funds in existing Hong Kong's pension funds were estimated to total about HK$200 billion.
The MPF scheme will require individual employees and employers to each contribute five percent of a monthly salary to a retirement fund.
Hong Kong's Legislative Council has passed framework legislation allowing its creation, but subsidiary legislation and regulations are being drafted.
These are expected to be ready by April. Leckie said he expected the MPF to start operating in the first half of 1998.
